late: The baker’s niece misses her ride. She brings the empty basket back after supper.
firstCost: Kip turns the work slip over. “I can run this home. I can't give the baker her morning back.”
secondCost: Kip taps the unpaid toll with his spoon. “They heard us. The cart still won't wait.”
turn: The flour on the thumbprint matches the open sack beside the warm oven.
humour: A sparrow has stolen the A in PEARS. Corvan now sells unusually expensive ears.

late: The river runner has gone. Imani finds two dry reeds for the reader on the late shift.
firstCost: Imani sets aside a place at dinner. “Tonight I'll be waiting for a reader who should be home.”
secondCost: The runner flexes a cramped thumb. “They can unpack it themselves. I carried it blind.”
turn: A seal left unbroken can still belong to somebody who never read what it closed.
humour: A clerk has labelled a bundle of spare labels. Imani is waiting to see where it ends.

late: The registrar puts the first slip away. Odile opens the family desk herself after dark.
firstCost: Odile rubs a key mark from her palm. “We can look. I had wanted one day without the questions.”
secondCost: The registrar shuts the early drawer. “I'll tell our visitor why she came here twice.”
turn: The tissue holds the shape of the loose slip after the ink on the file has dried.
humour: Frost has made a fine white moustache on the youngest registrar’s painted portrait. She insists it stays.

late: The first pilot has cast off. Ruan hangs a shore lamp for the evening crew.
firstCost: Ruan carries the spare lamp downstairs. “My trainee was supposed to have that light tonight.”
secondCost: The pilot ties a second knot. “Someone else gets the easy crossing. We test yours in dusk.”
turn: The late sound bounces from the shed exactly when the early card says to turn.
humour: A gull rings the test bell and waits for a fish. Nobody wants to tell it the grant has ended.

clock: Before the dawn watch lifts its blind
late: The dawn watcher folds the blind. The keeper at the creek makes a space at dusk.
firstCost: Ayla curls one cold foot into her coat. “Another watch. That's a song at home I won't hear.”
secondCost: The counter shrugs on the wet cloak. “One patrol has to carry both numbers now.”
turn: A second perch comes into sight once someone walks around the recorder rather than the nest.
humour: A bird imitates the sign for a quiet observer. Every observer immediately whispers about it.

clock: Before the jig goes back on the line
late: The day fitter takes the clamp away. A buyer stays late to see Corra’s evening trial.
firstCost: Corra picks up her lunch cloth. “I'll explain this one. She's lost enough time at this gate.”
secondCost: The apprentice puts on the heavy gloves. “They can use it today. I get to find the limit.”
turn: The guild stamp follows the test bench from job to job. The maker’s mark stays on the reverse.
humour: Harl’s measuring stick is labelled STICK. The apprentice is waiting for the guild to certify the string.

clock: Before the press takes its next sheet
late: The printer runs the first edition. A reader at the night desk must carry the correction.
firstCost: Mina puts a clean strip by the till. “Somebody has to ask every borrower to come back.”
secondCost: The printer fishes a letter from the ink. “We bought time with a whole shift of somebody's hands.”
turn: The press copies a stain as faithfully as a correction. Turn the source over before naming its author.
humour: The printer advertises a book called Quiet. The only advertisement squeaks in the wind.

clock: Before the last pilot takes the tide
late: The old pilot takes the tide without the order. Sora waits at the shore light for the next boat.
firstCost: Sora hangs a dry coat on a peg. “I promised that seat to my cousin. Your second witness needs it.”
secondCost: The pilot shifts a reef marker a handspan. “We'll make the crossing. I'll be the one who has to sound it.”
turn: The turn in the sung direction falls a beat after the turn on the printed chart.
humour: The chart cupboard squeaks in the same key as the ferry song. Sora has entered it as relief crew.

clock: Before the usher draws the aisle rope
late: The early audience takes its seats. Hari keeps the last aisle open for the night witness.
firstCost: Hari takes a seat out of the row. “A stranger will stand so your second witness can see.”
secondCost: The understudy smooths the empty cushion. “I get to explain the pause to a full house.”
turn: An empty chair seen from the wings has a folded visitor’s coat across the seat.
humour: The sandbag plays a tree in the matinee. It is the only cast member who has never asked for a bigger part.

clock: Before the grain goes under the awning
late: The market shutters come down. Dagny weighs the evening basket in a patch of borrowed light.
firstCost: Dagny knocks on the closed stall. “One weaver will be doing accounts over supper.”
secondCost: Tellen frees a grain from the pan. “Somebody at the short end of the queue gets the trial price.”
turn: Moving the grain into another basket moves the reading even when nobody adds any grain.
humour: Someone has priced the sign that says FREE SAMPLES. The samples are fine with this arrangement.

late: The first gate crew has signed out. Omi takes the message down to the people on the bottom step.
firstCost: Omi rolls a wet sleeve. “The faster bank gets a head start. I'll have to tell my neighbours why.”
secondCost: The caller goes back uphill. “We've agreed on the sound. There's one kitchen that can't hear it.”
turn: The same gate call reaches the second bank after the last person has left its meeting.
humour: A frog has occupied the public speaking cup. For the first time the meeting adjourns on a single croak.

clock: Before the route board is punched
late: The early queue takes its old route. The west-street porter waits for the late dispatch.
firstCost: The clerk rubs where the strap sat. “Someone on the long route just inherited a second walk.”
secondCost: A porter pockets the short ticket. “We can go now. I owe the blue house another visit.”
turn: The printed route still joins up when a doorstep is removed. The walker notices immediately.
humour: The device issues a waiting ticket to the person replacing the waiting tickets.

late: The early listener has gone home. Wren leaves the family a key to the evening booth.
firstCost: Wren brushes a spot from the earpiece. “I can protect that pause. They still had to come here to ask.”
secondCost: The listener holds out an open hand. “The index can go up. I'll be answering calls about the silence.”
turn: Turning the reel back far enough reveals a second voice asking for the recorder to wait.
humour: The sound box contains a perfect recording of somebody asking if the sound box is working.

clock: Before the last model crate is strapped
late: The ferry loads the first model. Ivo sends a second sample with the late carrier.
firstCost: Ivo folds the ribbon. “One gardener will water two trial rows so the rest of us can compare them.”
secondCost: The carrier sits on the strapped crate. “You've bought a quick trial with the last place on my boat.”
turn: The small shade changes one row that the original scoring frame left out of sight.
humour: The model shed contains a model model shed. Its builder has firmly declined a smaller commission.

clock: Before the witness chairs are carried in
late: The first witnesses sit down. The rail steward stays to carry the late slips to the second sitting.
firstCost: The steward lays a cup by the door. “The family gets another chance to speak. They have to live this evening twice.”
secondCost: A witness folds up a coat. “I can sign tonight. I can't promise the next village was ready.”
turn: The paper trail and the two water recordings put the same interval in two different hearings.
humour: Someone has put a name card on the chair marked Spare Chair. The clerk asks it to declare an interest.
